text:
Maya R.: Heads-up — we need to lock down the label/schema for the new runtime metrics feeding the routing + quota dashboards. Goal: final review before we push to prod next Tues.
Owen (infra): +1. can we please include cardinality constraints up front? last time a freeform label exploded a dashboard. :grimacing:
Dalia - Runtime: Agree. Proposal from runtime side: keep these labels only — route, model_id, deployment_env, region, quant_profile, batching (bool), quota_tier. No user IDs, no request IDs.
Samir (telemetry): That list looks good. A couple notes: map to OTel semantic keys where possible (service.name, deployment.environment). For Prom we should use snake_case labels. Also: define allowed value sets for model_id and quota_tier to bound cardinality.
Jess QA: How many distinct model_id values are we comfortable with in a single Prom label? Dashboards choked when a label had ~5k values last quarter.
Owen (infra): We should aim for <100 unique values per label on any high-cardinality metric. If a metric is high-cardinality by design, we split it to a separate export with sampling.
Maya R.: Concrete suggestion: whitelist models that appear in production (top X by QPS) as explicit model_id labels; for others, use model_family or "other" bucket. That keeps label cardinality bounded.
Dalia - Runtime: +1. For rollout experiments: use rollout_group label (can be small set like canary, control, stable). Keep rollout_id out of labels.
Samir (telemetry): Example Prom metric we recommend: 
```
# HELP redwood_runtime_request_duration_seconds request latency for runtime
# TYPE redwood_runtime_request_duration_seconds histogram
redwood_runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="text_gen",model_id="gptx-8b",deployment_env="prod",region="us-west-2",quant_profile="int8",batching="true",quota_tier="standard",le="0.1"} 42
```
Map to OTel attributes: 
```
"service.name": "redwood-runtime"
"deployment.environment": "prod"
"redwood.model_id": "gptx-8b"
"redwood.route": "text_gen"
"redwood.quant_profile": "int8"
"redwood.batch.enabled": "true"
"redwood.quota.tier": "standard"
```
Owen (infra): Small nit: prefer boolean labels as "true"/"false" strings in Prom (as above) — avoids downstream parsing issues.
Jess QA: We also need a name convention doc: prometheus metric names should be prefixed `redwood_` then subsystem (runtime/infra) and suffix type (gauge/counter/histogram). That makes dashboards easier to author.
Maya R.: Sounds good. One open question: model version vs model_id. model_version can be high-card if we include build hashes. Suggest only allow semantic versions (v1, v2) or omit entirely in labels. Put full version in logs/OTel attributes but not Prom label.
Dalia - Runtime: Agree — runtime will send model_version as attribute on traces for deep debugging, but Prom labels will carry model_id (stable, short) and model_family.
Samir (telemetry): For cardinality gating, propose a pipeline check: when new metric + label pair is added, a CI job verifies estimated cardinality over the last 7 days (sampling). If >500 unique, fail with guidance. We can make threshold configurable per metric category.
Owen (infra): +1 to CI check. Where does the whitelist live? repo? config service?
Maya R.: Let's keep it in the telemetry repo as YAML (easy to review in PR). Example: 
```yaml
metrics_whitelist:
  redwood_runtime_request_duration_seconds:
    allowed_labels:
      model_id: ["gptx-8b","gptx-2b","other"]
      quota_tier: ["standard","enterprise"]
```
Samir (telemetry): That works. I'll draft the CI job. It will sample metrics from our test cluster and estimate cardinality. If unknown metric, it warns and adds a TODO for an explicit whitelist entry.
Jess QA: Also need a doc for frontend folks — which label to use to group in dashboards. e.g., group by model_family not model_id for aggregated panels.
Dalia - Runtime: For rollout UX in console: use rollout_group and percent_traffic labels to compute canary health. Percent_traffic should NOT be a label (high cardinality); instead expose a separate gauge `redwood_rollout_traffic_percent{rollout_group="canary"}`.
Maya R.: Good point. Keep numeric, high-card values as metrics, not labels.
Owen (infra): One more: region label values should follow cloud-region canonical ids (us-west-2, eu-central-1). We'll add validation in exporter.
Samir (telemetry): I'll add a short mapping doc that shows Prom label name <-> OTel attribute name (snake_case -> dot separated). This will help SDKs and exporters remain consistent.
Maya R.: Action items: Samir to draft mapping + CI job (ETA Thu), Dalia to update runtime exporter to drop model_version label and send attributes (ETA Fri), Owen to add whitelist YAML stub in telemetry repo (ETA Wed), Jess to prepare dashboard grouping guidance (ETA Fri). Meeting to finalize Wednesday 9:30 PT — I'll send invite.
infra-bot: deploy-checklist: telemetry-ci job added to CI queue (run id: 8921).
Jess QA: Thanks — will review once Samir posts draft. :thumbsup:
Maya R.: Thanks everyone. If you have quick objections post them here, otherwise we'll take this plan to the all-metrics sync on Wed.
Owen (infra): No objections from infra.
Dalia - Runtime: No objections. Will start changes today.
Samir (telemetry): Will post PR with mapping and CI job details shortly.
Maya R.: End.
